text: Immediately after a perfect 90-degree RF pulse, the longitudinal magnetization is:
explanation: A perfect 90-degree pulse tips the net magnetization into the transverse plane.

text: Immediately after a perfect 90-degree RF pulse, transverse magnetization is:
explanation: The 90-degree pulse transfers the equilibrium longitudinal magnetization into the transverse plane.

text: What determines the amount of longitudinal magnetization tipped into the transverse plane?
explanation: The flip angle determines how far the net magnetization vector is rotated away from the longitudinal axis.

text: A 180-degree RF pulse ideally causes the net magnetization to:
options: Rotate completely into the transverse plane
explanation: A 180-degree pulse reverses the longitudinal magnetization direction.

text: As T1 relaxation progresses, longitudinal magnetization:
explanation: T1 relaxation restores longitudinal magnetization toward its equilibrium value.

text: As T2 relaxation progresses, transverse magnetization:
explanation: Loss of phase coherence causes transverse magnetization to decrease toward zero.

text: A 30-degree RF pulse produces what approximate relationship between longitudinal and transverse magnetization immediately after excitation?
explanation: A small flip angle tips only part of the longitudinal magnetization into the transverse plane.

text: Which flip angle completely transfers ideal equilibrium longitudinal magnetization into the transverse plane?
explanation: A 90-degree pulse rotates the longitudinal magnetization into the transverse plane.

text: Which flip angle reverses longitudinal magnetization without leaving a longitudinal component in the ideal case?
explanation: A 180-degree pulse rotates the longitudinal magnetization completely to the opposite longitudinal direction.

text: Immediately after a 90-degree RF pulse, the initial signal produced by coherent transverse magnetization is called:
explanation: The coherent transverse magnetization immediately after excitation generates a free induction decay signal.

text: Why does free induction decay decrease after RF excitation?
explanation: Transverse signal decreases as spins dephase due to microscopic interactions and magnetic field variations.

text: Which component contributes to the decay observed in a free induction decay signal?
explanation: Free induction decay is affected by both intrinsic T2 decay and additional dephasing from field inhomogeneity, collectively reflected by T2*.

text: Which sequence parameter primarily determines the timing between successive excitation pulses?
explanation: TR is the time between successive excitation pulses applied to the same slice or volume.

text: Which sequence parameter primarily determines the time from excitation to signal echo?
explanation: TE is the time between the excitation pulse and the peak of the measured echo.
